name: Acharya Narendra Dev College
awards: NAAC A grade; UGC "College with Potential for Excellence"
shortHistory: Acharya Narendra Dev College was established in 1991 by the University of Delhi as a co-educational institution in Govindpuri, South Delhi, and is named after the freedom fighter, educationist and socialist leader Acharya Narendra Dev. It was set up mainly to expand undergraduate science capacity in South Delhi at a time of rising demand for science seats. The college has since built particularly strong science departments and has been recognised by the UGC as a "College with Potential for Excellence." It maintains an active elected students' union with annual elections and is counted among the newer additions to DU's southern cluster of colleges.

name: Aditi Mahavidyalaya
shortHistory: Aditi Mahavidyalaya was established in 1994 by the Government of NCT of Delhi at Bawana in North West Delhi as a women's college, aimed at extending affordable undergraduate education into the capital's fast-growing outer districts. It offers programmes in arts, commerce and journalism, including a well-regarded Hindi Journalism honours course. The college is part of the wave of new government colleges opened across Delhi through the 1990s. It maintains an active students' union and continues to serve students from Bawana, Narela and the surrounding North West Delhi localities.

name: Ahilya Bai College of Nursing
awards: Recognised by the Indian Nursing Council
website: Listed via du.ac.in; no independent domain confirmed
shortHistory: Ahilya Bai College of Nursing is a specialised nursing institution affiliated with the University of Delhi, named after the eighteenth-century Maratha queen Ahilyabai Holkar, celebrated for her administration and philanthropy. It offers undergraduate and diploma-level nursing programmes, training professionals through clinical instruction linked to an associated hospital alongside classroom-based coursework in nursing science. The college forms part of DU's cluster of specialised medical and paramedical institutions rather than its liberal-arts colleges. Admission and curriculum follow the Indian Nursing Council framework in conjunction with DU's academic calendar.

name: Amar Jyoti Institute of Physiotherapy
awards: Recognised by the Rehabilitation Council of India
shortHistory: Amar Jyoti Institute of Physiotherapy is a specialised institute affiliated with the University of Delhi, offering degree programmes in physiotherapy, and grew out of the wider Amar Jyoti Charitable Trust's work in rehabilitation and disability services in Delhi. It combines classroom instruction with clinical training, preparing students for careers in physical rehabilitation and allied health. It is one of DU's smaller, specialised professional colleges rather than a general arts-and-science institution, maintaining its own academic administration while following DU's examination and degree-conferral system.

name: Aryabhatta College
foundingBody: University of Delhi (took over from the Ram Lal Anand Trust); formerly Ram Lal Anand College (Evening)
studentUnionStatus: Active - Students' Union; ratified constitution, advisory committee
shortHistory: Aryabhatta College was established in 1973 by the University of Delhi and was later renamed to honour the ancient Indian mathematician and astronomer Aryabhatta. It grew out of Delhi University's expansion of general-degree education in South Delhi and runs as a full day college offering undergraduate programmes in arts, commerce and science. It has developed a growing reputation in economics, computer science and commerce. The college maintains an active students' union and continues to expand its academic infrastructure within South Campus's institutional cluster.

name: Atma Ram Sanatan Dharma College (ARSD)
awards: NAAC A+ grade; UGC "College with Potential for Excellence"; MHRD "Star College"
shortHistory: Atma Ram Sanatan Dharma College was established in 1959 by the Sanatan Dharma Sabha, Delhi - the same organisation that founded Hindu College decades earlier - and is named after the philanthropist Atma Ram Chadha. Initially located in Paharganj, it relocated to Dhaula Kuan as part of Delhi University's expansion of South Campus. The college is particularly well known for its commerce and science departments and has been designated a "Star College" under the Ministry of Education's science scheme. Its alumni include prominent figures in business, banking and public administration, and it maintains a functioning students' union with periodic elections.

name: Ayurvedic & Unani Tibbia College
foundingBody: Municipal/princely-era patronage; now Government of NCT of Delhi
awards: Recognised under DU's Faculty of Ayurvedic & Unani Medicine
website: Listed via du.ac.in; no independent domain confirmed
shortHistory: Ayurvedic & Unani Tibbia College, founded in 1916, is one of Delhi's oldest institutions for traditional Indian systems of medicine, located in Karol Bagh. It offers degree programmes affiliated with DU's Faculty of Ayurvedic and Unani Medicine, training practitioners in Ayurveda and Unani therapeutics alongside modern clinical exposure. The college predates the University of Delhi itself, having been established under earlier municipal and princely patronage before its later affiliation. It runs attached hospital facilities for student clinical training and remains a distinctive part of DU's medical-education cluster, separate from its mainstream liberal-arts colleges.

name: Bhagini Nivedita College
shortHistory: Bhagini Nivedita College was established in 1993 by the Government of NCT of Delhi at Kair, near Najafgarh in South West Delhi, and is named after Sister Nivedita, the Irish-born disciple of Swami Vivekananda who devoted her life to Indian education and social reform. It was set up to extend undergraduate access to the rural and semi-urban population of South West Delhi, offering programmes in arts and commerce. It maintains a students' union and continues to serve a largely first-generation college-going student body from the Najafgarh belt.

name: Bharati College
shortHistory: Bharati College was established in 1971 by the Government of NCT of Delhi as a women's college in Janakpuri, West Delhi, founded to expand higher-education access for women in the rapidly developing West Delhi residential colonies. It offers undergraduate programmes across arts, commerce and science, with particular strength in commerce. The college maintains an active students' union and a range of departmental societies, continuing to serve a large student population drawn from Janakpuri, Uttam Nagar and neighbouring West Delhi localities.

name: Bhaskaracharya College of Applied Sciences (BCAS)
shortHistory: Bhaskaracharya College of Applied Sciences was established in 1995 by the Government of NCT of Delhi in Dwarka and is named after the twelfth-century Indian mathematician and astronomer Bhaskaracharya (Bhaskara II). It was founded specifically to expand capacity in applied and industry-oriented science education, distinguishing it from DU's more traditional liberal-arts-and-science colleges. It offers specialised undergraduate programmes such as applied physical sciences, biomedical science, instrumentation and computer science geared toward industry and research careers, and maintains active student governance and modern laboratory infrastructure.

name: Dr Bhim Rao Ambedkar College
shortHistory: Dr Bhim Rao Ambedkar College was established in 1991 by the Government of NCT of Delhi in Yamuna Vihar, North East Delhi, and is named after Dr B.R. Ambedkar, chief architect of the Indian Constitution and a lifelong campaigner for social justice. It was set up to extend undergraduate education to the densely populated Trans-Yamuna region, offering programmes in arts, commerce and science. It maintains an active students' union and has grown into one of the principal government colleges serving North East Delhi's student population.

name: Chacha Nehru Bal Chikitsalaya (Nursing)
awards: Recognised by the Indian Nursing Council
website: Listed via du.ac.in; no independent domain confirmed
shortHistory: Chacha Nehru Bal Chikitsalaya's associated nursing programme is affiliated with the University of Delhi and attached to a government children's hospital in Geeta Colony, East Delhi. Named after Jawaharlal Nehru, affectionately called "Chacha Nehru" by Indian schoolchildren, it trains nursing students with a focus on paediatric and general nursing care through hands-on clinical placement alongside classroom instruction. It forms part of DU's specialised health-sciences cluster rather than its general undergraduate colleges, with admissions following Indian Nursing Council norms in coordination with DU's academic calendar.

name: College of Art
awards: Recognised under DU's Faculty of Fine Arts
shortHistory: The College of Art was established in 1942 in Mandi House, Central Delhi, as a dedicated institution for fine arts education, administered by the Government of NCT of Delhi. It offers undergraduate and postgraduate degrees in painting, sculpture, applied art, graphic design and visual communication, and has trained generations of Indian artists, designers and art educators. It maintains galleries and studios used for student exhibitions, sits within Delhi's central cultural district alongside other performing- and visual-arts institutions, and continues to be one of India's most recognised government fine-arts colleges.

name: College of Nursing, Army Hospital (Research & Referral)
awards: Recognised by the Indian Nursing Council
website: Listed via du.ac.in; no independent domain confirmed
shortHistory: The College of Nursing at the Army Hospital (Research & Referral) is affiliated with the University of Delhi and administered under the Armed Forces Medical Services. Located within the Delhi Cantonment area, it trains undergraduate nursing students with a strong clinical component drawn from the tertiary-care military hospital to which it is attached. The college follows Indian Nursing Council standards alongside DU's degree and examination framework, largely serving defence-service dependants and civilian applicants seeking a nursing career with a strong clinical grounding.

name: College of Vocational Studies (CVS)
shortHistory: College of Vocational Studies was established in 1972 by the University of Delhi in Sheikh Sarai, South Delhi, as part of a national push toward vocational and industry-linked undergraduate education. It offers programmes combining conventional arts and commerce degrees with vocational and skill-based components such as office management, tourism and computer applications, and was among the pioneers of the vocational-education stream within DU. It maintains an active students' union and a curriculum emphasising employability alongside academic study, located near several other South Delhi DU colleges.

name: Daulat Ram College
awards: NAAC A grade; UGC "College with Potential for Excellence"
shortHistory: Daulat Ram College was established in 1960 through a private trust as a women's college in North Campus, named after the philanthropist and educationist Daulat Ram Gupta, whose family funded several Delhi University institutions. It grew into one of the university's leading women's colleges, with recognised strength in the sciences - particularly botany, zoology and chemistry - as well as commerce and the humanities, and has been recognised by the UGC as a "College with Potential for Excellence." Its alumnae include prominent scientists, administrators and media professionals, and the college maintains an active elected students' union along with a well-regarded annual cultural festival, Aarohan.

name: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya College (DDUC)
shortHistory: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya College was founded in 1990 by the University of Delhi in Dwarka, West Delhi, and is named after the political thinker Deen Dayal Upadhyaya, known for articulating the philosophy of "Integral Humanism." It was established as part of the university's ongoing expansion into the rapidly developing western suburbs of Delhi, offering undergraduate programmes across arts, commerce and science. The college maintains an active elected students' union and serves a growing student population drawn from Dwarka and the wider West and South West Delhi region.

name: Delhi College of Arts & Commerce (DCAC)
shortHistory: Delhi College of Arts & Commerce was established in 1987 by the Government of NCT of Delhi in Netaji Nagar, South Delhi, set up to expand commerce and humanities capacity in South Delhi at a time of rising demand for undergraduate seats. The college offers programmes in arts and commerce, with commerce (honours) among its most sought-after courses. It maintains an active students' union and a range of departmental societies, and its South Delhi location places it among DU's cluster of Netaji Nagar/Sarojini Nagar-area colleges.

name: Delhi Institute of Pharmaceutical Sciences and Research (DIPSAR)
awards: Recognised by the Pharmacy Council of India; NAAC accredited
shortHistory: Delhi Institute of Pharmaceutical Sciences and Research was established in 1964 by the Government of NCT of Delhi and is a specialised pharmacy institute affiliated with the University of Delhi. It offers undergraduate and postgraduate degrees in pharmaceutical sciences, training students for careers in drug research, manufacturing and clinical pharmacy. The institute maintains dedicated pharmaceutical laboratories distinct from DU's general-degree colleges, has built a reputation as one of India's stronger government pharmacy schools, and functions under DU's Faculty of Science framework for degree conferral.

name: Deshbandhu College
shortHistory: Deshbandhu College was established in 1952 by the Government of NCT of Delhi in Kalkaji, South Delhi, and is named after Chittaranjan Das, popularly known as "Deshbandhu" ("friend of the nation"), a prominent freedom-movement leader. It was set up to extend undergraduate education to South Delhi's expanding post-independence population, offering programmes in arts, commerce and science. It maintains an active elected students' union and remains one of the principal government colleges serving the Kalkaji-Govindpuri belt of South Delhi.

name: Durga Bai Deshmukh College of Special Education (Visual Impairment)
awards: Recognised by the Rehabilitation Council of India
website: Listed via du.ac.in; no independent domain confirmed
shortHistory: Durga Bai Deshmukh College of Special Education (Visual Impairment) is a specialised institute affiliated with the University of Delhi, focused on training special educators for children with visual impairment. It is named after Durgabai Deshmukh, the social reformer and freedom fighter who championed welfare and rehabilitation causes in independent India. The college offers degree and diploma programmes recognised by the Rehabilitation Council of India alongside DU's academic framework, combining classroom pedagogy training with practical teaching placements, and represents one of DU's smaller, mission-specific colleges within the special-education sector.

name: Dyal Singh College
shortHistory: Dyal Singh College traces its origin to a college founded in Lahore in 1910 by the Dyal Singh Trust Society, set up to continue the educational philanthropy of Sardar Dyal Singh Majithia, a nineteenth-century Punjabi philanthropist and founder of The Tribune newspaper. Following Partition in 1947, the original Lahore institution was lost to the new border, and the trust re-established the college in Delhi in 1959 on Lodhi Road, making it a clear example of post-Partition educational rehabilitation within Delhi University. The college offers programmes across arts, science and commerce and maintains an active elected students' union.

name: Dyal Singh College (Evening)
shortHistory: Dyal Singh College (Evening) was established in 1958 by the Dyal Singh Trust Society on the same Lodhi Road campus as its morning counterpart, to extend access to working students unable to attend daytime classes. It shares its founding rationale - continuing Sardar Dyal Singh Majithia's educational philanthropy after the loss of the original Lahore college at Partition - while operating with its own administration and students' union. It offers programmes largely in arts and commerce suited to employed and part-time students, and has played a role in making DU degrees accessible to non-traditional students in South Delhi.

name: Florence Nightingale College of Nursing
awards: Recognised by the Indian Nursing Council
website: Listed via du.ac.in; no independent domain confirmed
shortHistory: Florence Nightingale College of Nursing is affiliated with the University of Delhi and attached to Guru Teg Bahadur Hospital in East Delhi. Named after Florence Nightingale, the founder of modern nursing, it trains undergraduate nursing students through a combination of classroom instruction and hospital-based clinical practice, following Indian Nursing Council curriculum requirements alongside DU's degree-conferral system. It forms part of DU's East Delhi cluster of specialised medical and paramedical institutions and continues to supply trained nursing professionals to Delhi's government hospital system.

name: Gargi College
awards: NAAC A+ grade; UGC "College with Potential for Excellence"
shortHistory: Gargi College was established in 1967 by the University of Delhi as a women's college near Siri Fort in South Delhi, taking its name from Gargi Vachaknavi, the ancient Indian philosopher celebrated in the Upanishads for her scholarly debates with the sage Yajnavalkya. It was set up as part of the university's expansion of women's education in South Delhi during the 1960s and today offers a wide range of undergraduate programmes across arts, science and commerce. Gargi has been recognised by the UGC as a "College with Potential for Excellence," and its annual cultural festival, Reverie, is among the more prominent college festivals in Delhi. The college maintains an active elected students' union.

name: Hans Raj College
awards: NAAC A+ grade; UGC "College with Potential for Excellence"
shortHistory: Hans Raj College was founded in 1948 by the D.A.V. College Managing Committee to meet the surge in demand for higher education in the newly independent capital, and is named after Mahatma Hansraj, a leading figure of the Arya Samaj. Located in North Campus, it grew rapidly into one of the largest constituent colleges of Delhi University by student strength, with strong departments across science, commerce and the humanities, and has been recognised by the UGC as a "College with Potential for Excellence." Its notable alumni include figures in politics, cinema, sport and business, and it maintains an active elected students' union along with one of DU's largest annual cultural festivals.

name: Hindu College
foundingBody: Sanatan Dharma Sabha, with support from nationalist leaders
awards: NAAC A+ grade; UGC "College with Potential for Excellence"
shortHistory: Hindu College was established in 1899 by members of the Sanatan Dharma Sabha, with early support from figures associated with the nationalist movement, and is one of the four founding colleges of the University of Delhi when it was constituted in 1922. Located in North Campus opposite Miranda House, it grew through the early twentieth century into a centre of both academic excellence and nationalist student activity, and is today consistently ranked among the top arts, science and commerce colleges in India in NIRF rankings. It has been recognised by the UGC as a "College with Potential for Excellence" and holds NAAC's highest institutional grade. The campus remains a hub of debating societies, dramatics and an active, democratically elected students' union.

name: Holy Family College of Nursing
awards: Recognised by the Indian Nursing Council
website: Listed via du.ac.in; no independent domain confirmed
shortHistory: Holy Family College of Nursing is affiliated with the University of Delhi and attached to Holy Family Hospital in Okhla, South Delhi, a missionary-run hospital with a long history of healthcare service in the capital. The college trains undergraduate nursing students through classroom study combined with hospital-based clinical placements, following Indian Nursing Council standards in conjunction with DU's degree framework. It retains a values-based institutional character rooted in its founding hospital's tradition and continues to train nursing professionals for both hospital and community healthcare roles.

name: Indira Gandhi Institute of Physical Education & Sports Sciences (IGIPESS)
shortHistory: Indira Gandhi Institute of Physical Education & Sports Sciences was established in 1987 by the Government of NCT of Delhi in Vikaspuri, West Delhi, and is named after former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi. It is DU's dedicated institute for physical education, offering specialised undergraduate and postgraduate degrees in physical education and sports coaching, and maintains sports grounds, gymnasia and training facilities distinct from DU's general-degree colleges. It trains physical-education teachers and sports professionals for schools and sporting bodies across India and remains one of the few specialised sports-science institutions within the DU system.

name: Indraprastha College for Women
foundingBody: A group of pioneering educationists in Old Delhi
shortHistory: Indraprastha College for Women, founded in 1924, is one of the oldest women's colleges in Delhi and is named after Indraprastha, the legendary capital city of the Pandavas in the Mahabharata. It was established in Old Delhi and moved to its present campus near Kashmere Gate, close to the historic Delhi Gate area of North Campus. For nearly a century the college has been a pioneer in women's education in the city, building particular strength in the sciences and commerce alongside the humanities. It has been designated a UGC "Heritage College" and holds a strong NAAC grade, and it maintains an active elected students' union along with a long-running annual festival tradition.

name: Institute of Home Economics
website: Listed via du.ac.in; no independent domain confirmed
shortHistory: The Institute of Home Economics was established in 1958 as a women's college specialising in home science, located in South Delhi. It offers undergraduate and postgraduate degrees in food and nutrition, textiles and clothing, human development, and resource management, and has built a long-standing reputation in applied home-science education alongside Lady Irwin College, DU's other major home-science institution. It maintains dedicated laboratories for nutrition and textile research and continues to train graduates for careers in nutrition, design, early-childhood education and allied applied sciences.

name: Janki Devi Memorial College
shortHistory: Janki Devi Memorial College was established in 1959 through a private trust as a women's college near Sir Ganga Ram Hospital Marg, Rajinder Nagar, and is named after Janki Devi Bajaj, a Gandhian social reformer and freedom-movement participant known for her work in women's welfare and rural upliftment. The college offers undergraduate programmes in arts, commerce and science, maintains an active elected students' union and a range of departmental societies, and its central-west Delhi location makes it accessible to students from Karol Bagh, Patel Nagar and surrounding areas.

name: Jesus & Mary College (JMC)
foundingBody: Congregation of Jesus and Mary (Roman Catholic religious order)
awards: NAAC A+ grade; UGC "College with Potential for Excellence"
shortHistory: Jesus & Mary College was founded in 1968 by the Congregation of Jesus and Mary, a Roman Catholic religious institute with a long history of women's education in India, to provide values-based higher education for women in South Delhi's Chanakyapuri area. The college built strong programmes in commerce, economics and the humanities while retaining its Catholic minority institutional character under Article 30 of the Constitution. It has been recognised by the UGC as a "College with Potential for Excellence," and its notable alumnae include leaders in business, media and public administration; its compact, leafy South Campus location is close to several diplomatic missions.

name: Kalindi College
shortHistory: Kalindi College was established in 1967 by the Government of NCT of Delhi as a women's college in East Patel Nagar, West Delhi, and is named after Kalindi, the Sanskrit name for the river Yamuna. It was founded to expand women's higher education in West Delhi during a decade of rapid DU expansion, offering undergraduate programmes primarily in arts and commerce. It maintains an active students' union and a range of departmental and cultural societies, continuing to serve women students from Patel Nagar and the wider West Delhi area.

name: Kamala Nehru College (KNC)
awards: NAAC A grade; UGC "College with Potential for Excellence"
shortHistory: Kamala Nehru College was founded in 1964 by the University of Delhi as a women's college in South Delhi, named after Kamala Nehru, freedom fighter and wife of India's first Prime Minister, Jawaharlal Nehru. It was established during a period of substantial expansion in Delhi University's women's-education infrastructure through the 1960s, developing particularly strong programmes in the arts, commerce and psychology, and has been recognised by the UGC as a "College with Potential for Excellence." Its alumnae include notable figures in social work, academia and public life, and the college maintains an active elected students' union along with a lively tradition of theatre and debate societies.

name: Keshav Mahavidyalaya
shortHistory: Keshav Mahavidyalaya was established in 1994 by the University of Delhi in Pitampura, North West Delhi, and is named "Keshav" after an epithet of Lord Krishna, reflecting the cultural naming conventions common among DU colleges founded in this period. It was set up as part of a broader wave of new colleges established across Delhi in the 1990s to expand higher-education access in the rapidly urbanising outer districts. The college offers undergraduate programmes in arts, commerce and science, maintains an active students' union, and continues to serve students from Pitampura, Rohini and the wider North West Delhi region.

name: Kirori Mal College (KMC)
awards: NAAC A+ grade; UGC "College with Potential for Excellence" (2016)
studentUnionStatus: Active - Students' Union (morning & evening); annual elections
shortHistory: Kirori Mal College was founded in 1954 through the philanthropy of the Sri Kirori Mal Charitable Trust, established by a family of Sindhi businessmen, in part to serve refugee and migrant communities that had settled in Delhi after Partition. Named for the trust's founder, Lala Kirori Mal, the college quickly built a reputation for strong arts and science programmes and, especially, for its dramatics society and cultural life. It was recognised by the UGC as a "College with Potential for Excellence" in 2016, and its notable alumni include actors, writers and politicians such as Ajay Maken. Its North Campus location, opposite the Delhi University metro station, makes it one of the most centrally situated colleges in the university.

name: Lady Hardinge Medical College
foundingBody: Colonial-era government initiative, named for Lady Hardinge
awards: Recognised by the NMC (Medical Council); premier women's medical college
shortHistory: Lady Hardinge Medical College was established in 1916 by the colonial government as India's first medical college dedicated to training women doctors, named after Lady Hardinge, wife of the then Viceroy. Located in Central Delhi, it remains affiliated with the University of Delhi for undergraduate and postgraduate medical degrees, and is attached to Smt. Sucheta Kriplani Hospital and Kalawati Saran Children's Hospital for clinical training. It has produced generations of women physicians and remains one of India's most respected medical institutions, functioning under DU's Faculty of Medical Sciences framework.

name: Lady Irwin College
shortHistory: Lady Irwin College was founded in 1932 by the All India Women's Conference to pioneer higher education in Home Science for women in India, and was named after Lady Irwin, wife of the then Viceroy Lord Irwin. It was the first institution in the country to offer a degree course in Home Science, initially housed near the Viceregal Estate before moving to its present site on Sikandra Road. The college has played a foundational role in Indian research and pedagogy in nutrition, textiles and human development, and today also runs postgraduate and doctoral programmes. It functions under a Government of India body (Ministry of Women and Child Development) rather than as a purely DU-funded college, and maintains an active students' union with annual elections.

name: Lady Shri Ram College for Women (LSR)
foundingBody: Sriram family/LSR trust, in memory of Lady Shri Ram
awards: NAAC A++ grade; UGC "College with Potential for Excellence"
shortHistory: Lady Shri Ram College for Women was founded in 1956 by the Delhi-based Sriram industrial family in memory of Lady Shri Ram, wife of the industrialist and philanthropist Sir Shri Ram, and set out to provide women in newly independent India with an education of the highest standard. Located in South Delhi's Lajpat Nagar, it rapidly became one of the most prestigious women's colleges in the country, consistently ranked among India's top colleges for arts, commerce and social sciences. The college holds NAAC's highest grade and has been recognised by the UGC as a "College with Potential for Excellence." Its alumnae include leading figures in politics, business, journalism and the arts, and LSR maintains an active elected students' union and is known for its annual festival, Tarang.

name: Lakshmibai College
shortHistory: Lakshmibai College was founded in 1965 by the University of Delhi as a women's college in Ashok Vihar, North West Delhi, and is named after Rani Lakshmibai of Jhansi, the celebrated queen and military leader of the 1857 Indian Rebellion. The college was established as part of Delhi University's expansion of women's higher education into North West Delhi during the mid-1960s, offering undergraduate programmes primarily in arts and commerce. It maintains a students' union and continues to serve women students from Ashok Vihar and the surrounding North West Delhi area.

name: Maharaja Agrasen College
awards: NAAC A grade; UGC "College with Potential for Excellence"
shortHistory: Maharaja Agrasen College was established in 1994 by the Government of NCT of Delhi at Vasundhara Enclave, East Delhi, as part of a wave of new colleges set up in the 1990s to meet rising demand for higher education across the city. It is named after Maharaja Agrasen, a legendary king revered for his teachings on non-violence and cooperative social welfare, and offers undergraduate programmes in arts, commerce and science. It has been recognised by the UGC as a "College with Potential for Excellence," maintains a students' union, and serves a large student population from East Delhi, with a single campus despite occasional confusion in secondary sources.

name: Maharshi Valmiki College of Education
awards: Recognised by the National Council for Teacher Education (NCTE)
website: Listed via du.ac.in; no independent domain confirmed
shortHistory: Maharshi Valmiki College of Education was established in 1996 by the Government of NCT of Delhi in Geeta Colony, East Delhi, and is named after the sage Valmiki, traditionally credited as the author of the Ramayana. It is a specialised teacher-training college offering the Bachelor of Education (B.Ed.) degree affiliated with DU's Faculty of Education, training prospective school teachers through pedagogy coursework combined with school-based teaching practice. It serves aspiring educators primarily from East Delhi and represents one of DU's dedicated education colleges distinct from its general-degree institutions.

name: Maitreyi College
shortHistory: Maitreyi College was established in 1967 by the University of Delhi as a women's college in South Delhi's Chanakyapuri area, and is named after Maitreyi, the ancient philosopher known from the Brihadaranyaka Upanishad for her philosophical dialogue with the sage Yajnavalkya. It was founded as part of Delhi University's broader expansion of women's higher-education infrastructure across South Campus in the late 1960s, offering undergraduate programmes in the arts and sciences. The college maintains an active elected students' union and a range of departmental societies, and its alumnae include figures in academia, civil services and social work.

name: Mata Sundri College for Women
shortHistory: Mata Sundri College for Women was founded in 1967 by the Delhi Sikh Gurdwara Management Committee to expand higher-education opportunities for women, particularly from the Sikh community, and is named after Mata Sundri, wife of Guru Gobind Singh. Located in the Mandi House area of central Delhi alongside several other minority-run DU colleges, it offers programmes in arts, commerce and science while maintaining strong ties to Sikh religious and cultural values, including a campus gurdwara and Punjabi-language courses. It continues to expand its academic offerings and maintains an active students' union with annual elections.

name: Maulana Azad Institute of Dental Sciences
awards: Recognised by the Dental Council of India (now NMC-Dental)
shortHistory: Maulana Azad Institute of Dental Sciences was established in 2003 by the Government of NCT of Delhi, and is named after Maulana Abul Kalam Azad, India's first Education Minister. It is a dedicated dental college offering undergraduate (BDS) and postgraduate dental degrees affiliated with the University of Delhi, and is attached to Lok Nayak Hospital for clinical dental training. It has grown into one of Delhi's principal government dental colleges and functions under DU's Faculty of Medical Sciences for degree conferral and examinations.

name: Maulana Azad Medical College
awards: Recognised by the NMC (Medical Council); leading government medical college
studentUnionStatus: Resident doctors' association (no UG students' union)
shortHistory: Maulana Azad Medical College was established in 1956 by the Government of NCT of Delhi in Central Delhi, and is named after Maulana Abul Kalam Azad, the freedom-movement leader and India's first Education Minister. It is one of Delhi's premier government medical colleges, attached to Lok Nayak Hospital, Gobind Ballabh Pant Hospital and other major government hospitals for clinical training, offering MBBS and postgraduate medical degrees affiliated with the University of Delhi. It has trained generations of doctors who have gone on to leading positions in Indian medicine, and functions under DU's Faculty of Medical Sciences.

name: Miranda House
foundingBody: University of Delhi (Government), on the initiative of Vice-Chancellor Sir Maurice Gwyer
awards: NAAC A++ grade; repeatedly ranked India's No. 1 college (NIRF)
studentUnionStatus: Active - Students' Union/Student Council; annual elections
shortHistory: Miranda House was established on 8 February 1948 as the University of Delhi's first women's college, founded on the initiative of Vice-Chancellor Sir Maurice Gwyer to expand women's access to higher education in the newly independent nation. Built on part of the Viceregal Estate grounds in North Campus, it rapidly became one of the country's foremost institutions for science and humanities education for women. Its name is drawn from Miranda in Shakespeare's The Tempest, reflecting Gwyer's own literary inclination. Miranda House has for several consecutive years been ranked India's top college in NIRF rankings and holds NAAC's highest A++ grade, maintaining an active, elected Student Council and a wide network of academic and cultural societies.

name: Motilal Nehru College
shortHistory: Motilal Nehru College was established in 1964 by the University of Delhi in South Campus, and is named after Motilal Nehru, the freedom-movement leader and father of Jawaharlal Nehru. It was founded as part of Delhi University's 1960s expansion of South Campus, offering undergraduate programmes in arts, commerce and science, and has built a particular reputation in sports and athletics alongside its academic programmes. It maintains an active elected students' union and continues to be one of the well-established colleges within DU's South Campus cluster.

name: Motilal Nehru College (Evening)
shortHistory: Motilal Nehru College (Evening) was established in 1965 on the same South Campus premises as its morning counterpart, to extend access to working students unable to attend daytime classes. It shares its founding rationale and namesake, Motilal Nehru, with the morning college, while operating as a distinct institution with its own administration and students' union. It offers programmes largely in arts and commerce suited to the schedules of employed and part-time students, and has played a role in making DU degrees accessible to non-traditional students in South Delhi.

name: University College of Medical Sciences (UCMS)
foundingBody: Delhi Administration/Government of NCT of Delhi
studentUnionStatus: Resident doctors' association (no UG-style students' union)
shortHistory: University College of Medical Sciences was established in 1971 by the Delhi Administration in Dilshad Garden, East Delhi, as a constituent medical college of the University of Delhi. It is attached to Guru Teg Bahadur Hospital for clinical training and offers MBBS and postgraduate medical degrees, having built a strong reputation in medical research and community-medicine training. It serves as one of the principal government medical colleges catering to East Delhi's population and functions under DU's Faculty of Medical Sciences.

name: Nehru Homoeopathic Medical College & Hospital
awards: Recognised by the National Commission for Homoeopathy
website: Listed via du.ac.in; no independent domain confirmed
shortHistory: Nehru Homoeopathic Medical College & Hospital was established in 1967 by the Government of NCT of Delhi, and is named after Jawaharlal Nehru, India's first Prime Minister. It is DU's dedicated institution for homoeopathic medical education, offering the Bachelor of Homoeopathic Medicine and Surgery (BHMS) degree under DU's Faculty of Homoeopathic Medicine, and maintains an attached hospital used for student clinical training. It represents one of only two colleges within DU's affiliated systems of alternative medicine, alongside the Ayurvedic and Unani college, and continues to train practitioners for India's licensed homoeopathic sector.

name: P.G.D.A.V. College
foundingBody: D.A.V. College Trust and Management Society
shortHistory: P.G.D.A.V. College - formally Pannalal Girdharlal Dayanand Anglo-Vedic College - was founded in 1957 by the D.A.V. College Trust and Management Society, part of the wider network of Dayanand Anglo-Vedic institutions rooted in the Arya Samaj movement, and is named after the philanthropist Pannalal Girdharlal, a benefactor of the DAV movement. The college was set up as part of Delhi University's post-independence expansion into South Delhi and offers programmes in arts, commerce and science. It maintains an active elected students' union and continues to serve a large student body from South Delhi and neighbouring areas.

name: P.G.D.A.V. College (Evening)
foundingBody: D.A.V. College Trust and Management Society
shortHistory: P.G.D.A.V. College (Evening) was established in 1958, a year after its morning counterpart, on the same South Delhi campus, by the D.A.V. College Trust and Management Society. It was set up to extend access to working students unable to attend daytime classes, sharing its founding rationale and Arya Samaj heritage with the morning college. It offers programmes largely in arts and commerce suited to employed and part-time students, maintains its own administration and students' union, and continues to serve non-traditional students from South Delhi.

name: Pt. Deendayal Upadhyaya Institute for the Physically Handicapped
awards: Recognised by the Rehabilitation Council of India
website: Listed via du.ac.in; no independent domain confirmed
shortHistory: Pt. Deendayal Upadhyaya Institute for the Physically Handicapped is a Government of NCT of Delhi institution affiliated with the University of Delhi, offering specialised education, vocational training and rehabilitation programmes for persons with physical disabilities. It is named after Deen Dayal Upadhyaya, the political thinker known for his philosophy of "Integral Humanism," and combines classroom instruction with assistive-technology training and vocational skill-building. It represents one of DU's mission-specific institutions within the disability-services and special-education sector, working alongside DU's other special-education colleges to expand access for students with disabilities.

name: Rajdhani College
shortHistory: Rajdhani College was founded in 1964 by the University of Delhi in Raja Garden, West Delhi, its name ("Rajdhani," meaning "capital") reflecting its location in the national capital. The college was established during a phase of rapid expansion of Delhi University's West Delhi presence, aimed at serving the area's growing population, and offers undergraduate programmes in arts, commerce and science. It maintains a students' union and serves students primarily from West Delhi's residential colonies, in a part of the city with a significant concentration of DU colleges, including its near neighbour, Shivaji College.

name: Rajkumari Amrit Kaur College of Nursing (RAK)
foundingBody: Ministry of Health, Government of India, with support from the Indian Red Cross
awards: NAAC A grade; recognised by the Indian Nursing Council; a WHO Collaborating Centre
shortHistory: Rajkumari Amrit Kaur College of Nursing was founded in 1946, in the final years before independence, by the Ministry of Health with support from the Indian Red Cross, to address a severe shortage of trained nurses in India. It is named after Rajkumari Amrit Kaur, independent India's first Health Minister and a prominent participant in the freedom movement, and is widely regarded as India's first college of nursing, having trained generations of nursing professionals. The college has been designated a WHO Collaborating Centre for Nursing and offers undergraduate and postgraduate nursing degrees affiliated with the University of Delhi.

name: Ram Lal Anand College
shortHistory: Ram Lal Anand College was established in 1964 by the University of Delhi in South Campus, and is named after Rai Bahadur Ram Lal Anand, a philanthropist associated with the college's founding trust. It was set up as part of Delhi University's 1960s expansion of South Campus and offers undergraduate programmes across arts, commerce and science, having built strength in commerce and science alongside a lively cultural and sporting life. It maintains an active elected students' union and continues to be a well-regarded college within DU's South Campus cluster.

name: Ramanujan College
shortHistory: Ramanujan College was established in 2010 by the Government of NCT of Delhi in Kalkaji, South Delhi, making it one of the newest colleges in the DU system. It is named after Srinivasa Ramanujan, the self-taught Indian mathematician celebrated for his contributions to number theory and mathematical analysis, and offers undergraduate programmes in commerce, economics and computer science, with strong placement-oriented commerce and management courses. It has quickly built a reputation for skill-based and industry-linked education, maintaining an active students' union and continuing to expand its academic infrastructure.

name: Ramjas College
foundingBody: D.A.V. College Trust and Management Society (rooted in the Arya Samaj movement)
studentUnionStatus: Active - Students' Union/"House of Councils"; annual elections
shortHistory: Ramjas College was founded in 1917 in memory of the philanthropist Rai Kedar Nath's father Lala Ramjas, under the D.A.V. College Trust and Management Society associated with the Arya Samaj reform movement, and was among the founding colleges when the University of Delhi was established in 1922. The college is historically significant as the site of one of India's earliest student strikes and has a long tradition of student political activism, debate and literary societies; its current North Campus building was constructed in the early 1950s. Ramjas has strong programmes across arts, commerce and science, and its alumni include noted economists, journalists and public figures, with an active elected students' body alongside numerous departmental and cultural societies.

name: Satyawati College
shortHistory: Satyawati College was established in 1972 by the University of Delhi as part of the university's expansion into North West Delhi, and is named after Satyawati Devi, a freedom fighter associated with the independence movement in the Delhi region. It was set up to extend accessible higher education to the growing residential colonies of North West Delhi, including Ashok Vihar and surrounding areas, offering undergraduate programmes in arts, commerce and science. A separate evening college on the same campus was established in 1973 to further extend access to working students, and the college maintains an active elected students' union.

name: Satyawati College (Evening)
shortHistory: Satyawati College (Evening) was established in 1973 on the same Ashok Vihar campus as its morning counterpart, specifically to serve working students unable to attend daytime classes. It shares its founding rationale and namesake, freedom fighter Satyawati Devi, with the morning college, while operating with its own administration and students' union. It offers programmes largely in arts and commerce suited to employed and part-time students, and has played a role in making DU degrees accessible to non-traditional students in North West Delhi.

name: School of Open Learning (SOL)
studentUnionStatus: Not a physical undergraduate students' union (distance-education body)
shortHistory: The School of Open Learning was established in 1962 by the University of Delhi, originally as the School of Correspondence and Continuing Education, to provide distance and non-formal higher education. It is not a physical undergraduate college in the conventional sense but a university-wide distance-education body with headquarters near North Campus and study centres across Delhi. SOL offers undergraduate and postgraduate degrees to students who cannot attend regular DU colleges, using a mix of self-study material, personal contact programmes and, increasingly, online delivery, and serves one of the largest distance-learner populations of any Indian university body.

name: School of Rehabilitation Sciences
awards: Recognised by the Rehabilitation Council of India
website: Listed via du.ac.in; no independent domain confirmed
shortHistory: The School of Rehabilitation Sciences is a specialised institute affiliated with the University of Delhi, offering degree programmes in rehabilitation-related disciplines such as physiotherapy and occupational therapy. It combines classroom instruction with clinical placements at partner hospitals and rehabilitation centres, forming part of DU's smaller cluster of allied-health and rehabilitation-focused institutions. It follows the relevant professional council's curriculum requirements alongside DU's degree-conferral system, training practitioners who go on to work in hospital, community and disability-rehabilitation settings.

name: Shaheed Bhagat Singh College (SBSC)
shortHistory: Shaheed Bhagat Singh College was founded in 1967 by the University of Delhi at Sheikh Sarai in South Delhi, and is named after the revolutionary freedom fighter Bhagat Singh, executed by the British colonial government in 1931 at the age of 23. The college was established during a period of significant expansion of South Campus, reflecting a broader national practice of naming public institutions after independence-movement figures, and offers programmes primarily in arts and commerce. A separate evening college on the same campus was established in 1973, and the college maintains an active elected students' union, continuing to draw on its namesake's legacy in its institutional culture.

name: Shaheed Bhagat Singh College (Evening)
shortHistory: Shaheed Bhagat Singh College (Evening) was established in 1973 on the same Sheikh Sarai campus as its morning counterpart, to serve working students unable to attend daytime classes. It shares its founding rationale and namesake, revolutionary freedom fighter Bhagat Singh, with the morning college, while operating with its own administration and students' union. It offers programmes largely in arts and commerce suited to employed and part-time students, and has played a role in making DU degrees accessible to non-traditional students in South Delhi.

name: Shaheed Rajguru College of Applied Sciences for Women
shortHistory: Shaheed Rajguru College of Applied Sciences for Women was established in 1989 by the Government of NCT of Delhi in Vasundhara Enclave, East Delhi, and is named after Shivaram Rajguru, the revolutionary freedom fighter executed alongside Bhagat Singh in 1931. It is a women's college with a particular focus on the applied sciences, offering undergraduate programmes in subjects such as biomedical science, food technology and computer science alongside conventional science degrees, set up to expand science-education access for women in East Delhi. It maintains an active students' union and continues to serve a large student population from the Trans-Yamuna area.

name: Shaheed Sukhdev College of Business Studies (SSCBS)
shortHistory: Shaheed Sukhdev College of Business Studies was established in 1987 by the Government of NCT of Delhi as a specialised management and commerce college, and is named after Sukhdev Thapar, the revolutionary freedom fighter executed alongside Bhagat Singh and Rajguru in 1931. The college offers highly competitive undergraduate programmes in business economics, financial investment analysis and management studies, and has built a strong placement record, regarded as one of DU's premier commerce-oriented colleges. It maintains active student governance and a strong corporate-relations and placement cell, drawing applicants from across India for its specialised business programmes.

name: Shivaji College
shortHistory: Shivaji College was established in 1961 by the University of Delhi in Raja Garden, West Delhi, and is named after Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj, the seventeenth-century Maratha ruler celebrated for founding an independent Maratha kingdom. The college was founded during a decade of substantial growth for Delhi University, as new colleges were added across the city to accommodate the post-independence baby-boom generation reaching college age. It offers undergraduate programmes across arts, commerce and science, maintains active student governance and a range of departmental societies, and continues to serve students from West Delhi and neighbouring areas.

name: Shri Ram College of Commerce (SRCC)
awards: NAAC A++ grade; India's top-ranked commerce college (NIRF)
shortHistory: Shri Ram College of Commerce was established in 1926 by the Government of NCT of Delhi in North Campus, and is named after the industrialist and philanthropist Sir Shri Ram, whose family also founded Lady Shri Ram College. It is India's top-ranked commerce college, offering highly competitive undergraduate programmes in commerce and economics, and has produced generations of business leaders, economists and civil servants, consistently recording some of the highest cut-offs and placement packages in the country. It maintains a large, active students' union and a wide array of professional societies, and its North Campus location places it at the heart of DU's oldest academic cluster.

name: Shyam Lal College
shortHistory: Shyam Lal College was established in 1964 in Shahdara, East Delhi, as part of Delhi University's expansion to serve the growing population east of the Yamuna, and is named after the educationist Lala Shyam Lal. The college was founded to bring accessible higher education to working-class and government-employee families in East Delhi who previously had to travel across the river to North or South Campus colleges. It offers undergraduate programmes in commerce, arts and science, and a separate evening college on the same campus was established in 1969. The college maintains an active students' union with annual elections and remains one of the principal government colleges serving East Delhi.

name: Shyam Lal College (Evening)
shortHistory: Shyam Lal College (Evening) was established in 1969 on the same Shahdara campus as its morning counterpart, Shyam Lal College, specifically to serve working students unable to attend daytime classes. It shares its founding rationale with the morning college - expanding higher-education access in East Delhi - but operates as a distinct college with its own administration, faculty and students' union. It offers programmes largely in arts and commerce, suited to the schedules of employed and part-time students, and has played a significant role in making DU degrees accessible to non-traditional students in East Delhi.

name: Shyama Prasad Mukherji College for Women
shortHistory: Shyama Prasad Mukherji College for Women was established in 1969 by the Government of NCT of Delhi in Punjabi Bagh, West Delhi, and is named after Syama Prasad Mookerjee, the politician and founder of the Bharatiya Jana Sangh. It was founded to extend higher-education access for women in West Delhi's expanding residential colonies, offering undergraduate programmes in arts, commerce and science. It maintains an active students' union and a range of departmental societies, continuing to serve women students from Punjabi Bagh and neighbouring West Delhi localities.

name: Sri Aurobindo College
studentUnionStatus: Active - Students' Council; published election schedule
shortHistory: Sri Aurobindo College was established in 1972 by the University of Delhi in Malviya Nagar, South Delhi, timed to the birth centenary of the philosopher, poet and yogi Sri Aurobindo, after whom it is named. The college was founded to extend Delhi University's presence into the developing Malviya Nagar and Qutab Institutional Area, near the Sri Aurobindo Ashram and IIT Delhi, offering undergraduate programmes across arts, science and commerce and is particularly noted for its Sanskrit department. A distinct evening college on the same campus was established in 1984, admitting women students from 1988, and the college maintains an active Students' Council with elections following a published annual schedule.

name: Sri Aurobindo College (Evening)
shortHistory: Sri Aurobindo College (Evening) was established in 1984 on the same Malviya Nagar campus as its morning counterpart, to extend access to working students, and began admitting women students from 1988. It shares its founding rationale and namesake, the philosopher Sri Aurobindo, with the morning college, while operating with its own administration and students' body. It offers programmes largely in arts and commerce suited to employed and part-time students, and has played a role in making DU degrees accessible to non-traditional students in South Delhi, continuing to serve the Malviya Nagar and Qutab Institutional Area community.

name: Sri Guru Gobind Singh College of Commerce (SGGSCC)
shortHistory: Sri Guru Gobind Singh College of Commerce was founded in 1984 by the Delhi Sikh Gurdwara Management Committee in Pitampura, North West Delhi, and is named after Guru Gobind Singh, the tenth Sikh Guru, remembered for establishing the Khalsa and for his emphasis on equality and selfless service. As a specialised commerce college it was set up to meet growing demand for business and finance education and has built a strong reputation in B.Com (Honours) and related programmes. It represents one of several DSGMC-run institutions within Delhi University combining academic focus with the Sikh community's commitment to education, maintaining active student governance and serving students from Pitampura, Rohini and surrounding areas.

name: Sri Guru Nanak Dev Khalsa College
shortHistory: Sri Guru Nanak Dev Khalsa College was established in 1973 by the Delhi Sikh Gurdwara Management Committee in Dev Nagar, Karol Bagh, and is named after Guru Nanak Dev, the founder of Sikhism. It was set up to extend higher education to the Sikh community and the wider public in Central Delhi, complementing DSGMC's other DU colleges. The college offers undergraduate programmes in arts, commerce and science while maintaining its Sikh institutional character, including a campus gurdwara, and maintains an active students' union serving students from Karol Bagh and the surrounding Central Delhi area.

name: Sri Guru Tegh Bahadur Khalsa College (SGTB Khalsa)
awards: NAAC A grade; UGC "College with Potential for Excellence"
shortHistory: Sri Guru Tegh Bahadur Khalsa College was founded in 1951 by the Delhi Sikh Gurdwara Management Committee to serve the educational needs of the Sikh community and the wider public in the years following Partition. It is named after Guru Tegh Bahadur, the ninth Sikh Guru, revered for sacrificing his life in defence of religious freedom. Initially located in the Dev Nagar area, the college later moved to its present North Campus site along the ridge, developing strong programmes in the sciences, commerce and humanities while retaining its Sikh institutional character, including a campus gurdwara. It maintains an active students' union and a well-known college magazine and NCC unit.

name: Sri Venkateswara College
foundingBody: Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD), in partnership with the Government of India
awards: NAAC A grade (2022 cycle); UGC "College with Potential for Excellence"
shortHistory: Sri Venkateswara College was founded in 1961 by the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams, the trust that administers the Tirupati temple, in a distinctive government-trust partnership model, and is named after Lord Venkateswara. Located near Dhaula Kuan in South Campus, the college has built a strong reputation particularly in the physical sciences, including physics, chemistry and mathematics, alongside programmes in commerce and the humanities, and has been recognised by the UGC as a "College with Potential for Excellence." The college runs an active elected Students' Council, with results published annually; its temple-trust funding model makes it somewhat distinct in governance from purely government- or university-maintained DU colleges.

name: St. Stephen's College
awards: NAAC A+ (Cycle 3); UGC "College with Potential for Excellence"
studentUnionStatus: Active - St. Stephen's College Union; elections held annually; constitution available on college website
shortHistory: Founded in 1881 by the Anglican Church Missionary Society, St. Stephen's College is one of the oldest and most prestigious colleges in Delhi. Established during the British colonial era, it was named after Saint Stephen, the first Christian martyr. The college was originally located near Kashmere Gate before moving to its current campus in North Campus. It has consistently been ranked among the top colleges in India for arts and sciences. The college maintains its Christian character while welcoming students of all faiths. Its alumni include numerous prominent figures in politics, civil services, academia, and the arts. The college union is active and follows a democratic election process. The campus features heritage architecture and a vibrant intellectual culture.

name: Swami Shraddhanand College
shortHistory: Swami Shraddhanand College was established in 1967 by the Government of NCT of Delhi in Alipur, on the far northern edge of Delhi, and is named after Swami Shraddhanand, the Arya Samaj reformer and freedom-movement figure. It was set up to extend higher education to Delhi's then-rural northern periphery, offering undergraduate programmes in arts, commerce and science. It maintains a students' union and serves students from Alipur, Narela and the surrounding North West Delhi countryside, remaining one of DU's more geographically outlying colleges.

name: Vivekananda College
shortHistory: Vivekananda College was founded in 1970 by the University of Delhi in Vivek Vihar, East Delhi, and is named after Swami Vivekananda, the philosopher-monk who introduced Vedanta and yoga to Western audiences. The college was established at a time of substantial population growth in East Delhi driven by migration from neighbouring states, intended to extend affordable higher education to that expanding population, offering undergraduate programmes across arts, commerce and science. It has contributed significantly to educational access and social mobility in East Delhi, maintaining an active elected students' union as one of the principal government degree colleges serving the Trans-Yamuna area.

name: Zakir Husain Delhi College
shortHistory: Zakir Husain Delhi College traces its roots to 1792, making it the oldest college in Delhi, originally established as Delhi College before being renamed after Dr Zakir Husain, former President of India and a noted educationist. Located near Ajmeri Gate in Central Delhi, it has a long history spanning the late Mughal, colonial and post-independence periods, including a period of closure and revival in the nineteenth century. The college offers undergraduate programmes in arts, commerce and science, maintains an active students' union, and its deep historical roots make it a distinctive institution within Delhi University's affiliated system.

name: Zakir Husain Delhi College (Evening)
shortHistory: Zakir Husain Delhi College (Evening), also known as the Zakir Husain Post Graduate Evening College, was established in 1958 on the same Ajmeri Gate campus as its historic morning counterpart, to extend access to working students. It shares its namesake, Dr Zakir Husain, and its central Delhi location with the main college, while operating with its own administration and students' union. It offers programmes largely in arts and commerce suited to employed and part-time students, and has played a role in making DU degrees accessible to non-traditional students in Central Delhi.

name: Vallabhbhai Patel Chest Institute (VPCI)
foundingBody: University of Delhi, funded by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
awards: Recognised postgraduate/doctoral (MD, DM, Ph.D.) research institute
shortHistory: The Vallabhbhai Patel Chest Institute is a postgraduate medical institute devoted to chest and pulmonary diseases, located in the heart of DU's North Campus. Its foundation stone was laid by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel in 1949, growing out of a wartime diploma course in chest diseases run through Lady Hardinge Medical College, and it was formally opened in 1953 by Health Minister Rajkumari Amrit Kaur. It is a constituent institution of the University of Delhi, maintained under university statute and funded by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, offering postgraduate (MD), doctoral (DM) and Ph.D. programmes in pulmonary medicine and allied sciences such as physiology, pharmacology and microbiology. It runs its own attached hospital and hostel (Patel Niwas) and remains one of India's foremost centres for chest-disease research and training.

name: Netaji Subhash Institute of Technology (NSIT)
foundingBody: Delhi Administration (now Netaji Subhas University of Technology)
awards: Now an independent, self-accrediting university (not NAAC-rated as a DU college)
studentUnionStatus: Not applicable - separate university's own student body
shortHistory: Netaji Subhash Institute of Technology still appears as a link on DU's own colleges page but is included here only for completeness and accuracy, not as a currently affiliated college. Founded in 1983 as a Delhi Administration engineering college and long affiliated to the University of Delhi, NSIT was converted by an Act of the Delhi Legislative Assembly into the independent Netaji Subhas University of Technology (NSUT) in 2018. It now awards its own degrees and sets its own admissions, with no ongoing DU affiliation - its continued presence on du.ac.in's colleges listing appears to be an outdated link rather than a reflection of its current status. Prospective students should treat NSIT/NSUT as a separate university, not a DU college.

name: National Institute of Health & Family Welfare (NIHFW)
foundingBody: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (autonomous apex institute)
awards: WHO Collaborating Centre; recognised public-health training institute
studentUnionStatus: Not a UG students' union (postgraduate/officer-training institute)
shortHistory: The National Institute of Health & Family Welfare was established in 1977 through the merger of the National Institute of Health Administration and Education and the National Institute of Family Planning. It is an autonomous apex institute under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, located in Munirka, South Delhi, and is affiliated with the University of Delhi's Faculty of Medical Sciences for its degree programmes. NIHFW offers the MD in Community Health Administration, postgraduate diplomas in health and hospital administration, a Master of Public Health, and doctoral research, functioning as India's principal training and think-tank institute for public-health administration and family-welfare policy. It also serves as a WHO Collaborating Centre and trains serving government health officers alongside its degree students.

name: Kasturba Hospital
awards: Recognised for MD/Diploma in Obstetrics & Gynaecology, Diploma in Child Health
studentUnionStatus: Resident doctors' association (no UG students' union)
website: Listed via du.ac.in; no independent domain confirmed
shortHistory: Kasturba Hospital, one of Asia's larger maternity and women's hospitals, was established in 1905 in Darya Ganj, near Jama Masjid in Old Delhi, and today operates under the Municipal Corporation of Delhi. For its postgraduate medical programmes it is affiliated with the University of Delhi's Faculty of Medical Sciences, offering the MD and Diploma in Obstetrics & Gynaecology and the Diploma in Child Health, alongside DNB courses; its separate nursing programme is affiliated with a different university. The hospital's high delivery volume gives postgraduate trainees unusually intensive clinical exposure in maternal and child health, and it represents one of DU's oldest hospital-based teaching affiliations, predating the university itself by seventeen years.

name: Institute of Human Behaviour & Allied Sciences (IHBAS)
foundingBody: Ministry of Health / Government of NCT of Delhi (established under Supreme Court direction)
awards: Delhi's State Mental Health Authority; WHO-linked mental-health centre
studentUnionStatus: Not a UG students' union (postgraduate medical institute)
shortHistory: The Institute of Human Behaviour & Allied Sciences was established in 1993 under the direction of the Supreme Court of India, transforming the colonial-era Hospital for Mental Diseases, Shahdara into a modern centre for psychiatric and neurological treatment, training and research. Located in Dilshad Garden, East Delhi, it is an autonomous body jointly funded by the central Ministry of Health and the Government of NCT of Delhi, and is affiliated with the University of Delhi for its postgraduate medical programmes. IHBAS offers the MD in Psychiatry, DM in Neurology, M.Phil in Clinical Psychology, M.Sc. in Psychiatric Nursing and doctoral research across mental-health disciplines, and also serves as Delhi's State Mental Health Authority, among the largest mental-health treatment campuses in the world by patients served.

name: G.B. Pant Hospital (GIPMER)
awards: Recognised jointly by the NMC and UGC as a postgraduate institute
studentUnionStatus: Resident doctors' association (no UG students' union)
website: Listed via du.ac.in; no independent domain confirmed
shortHistory: Govind Ballabh Pant Hospital, now formally the G.B. Pant Institute of Postgraduate Medical Education & Research (GIPMER), had its foundation stone laid in 1961 and was commissioned by Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru in 1964, near Raj Ghat in Central Delhi. It is a constituent postgraduate college of the University of Delhi, recognised jointly by the Medical Council of India (now NMC) and the UGC, offering only postgraduate and doctoral degrees (MD, DM, M.Ch) rather than an MBBS programme. The hospital has grown from an initial 229 beds to more than 700, and is internationally recognised for cardiology, neurosurgery, gastroenterology and psychiatry, working closely with the neighbouring Maulana Azad Medical College for clinical training.

name: All India Institute of Ayurveda (AIIA)
awards: National apex Ayurveda institute; recognised by the Central Council of Indian Medicine
shortHistory: The All India Institute of Ayurveda was formally established on 12 November 2014 in Sarita Vihar, South Delhi, as India's apex autonomous institute for Ayurveda under the Ministry of AYUSH, though its origins trace back to a proposal announced in 2000 and a cornerstone laid in 2007. It is affiliated with the University of Delhi for its academic degree programmes, offering the Bachelor of Ayurvedic Medicine and Surgery (BAMS) alongside numerous postgraduate and doctoral courses across Ayurvedic specialisations. The institute runs a 200-bed referral hospital integrating traditional Ayurvedic practice with modern clinical infrastructure for teaching and research, and also houses interdisciplinary research laboratories and an international collaboration centre for Ayurveda, representing DU's newest and most specialised affiliated institution in the Indian systems of medicine.
